messages.subject: scale colour question
parts:
Hi all,

Simple question (aren't they always?)

Hadley kindly helped me to set this up a long time ago, during a break
from a lecture, but having trouble with simple parameter switches now.

What's going on here? Take a table like that formed by the simple
code:

t <- c(6,12,18,6,12,18)
tend <- c(12,18,19,12,18,19)
act <- c("?","on","?","off","on","off")
d <- c(1,1,1,2,2,2)
inc <- data.frame(d,t,act,tend)

Run this code:

qplot(xmin=t, xmax=tend, ymin=d-0.45, ymax=d+0.45, data=inc,
geom="rect", fill=act) + scale_y_reverse("Day", breaks = 1:2) +
scale_x_continuous("Time") + scale_fill_grey(name = "Activity", breaks
= c("?","off","on"), labels = c("Not recorded", "Off nest", "On
Nest"))

And get a nice looking figure.

However, if I wanted to do something like change the colors on the
bars, I'd figure something like this should work:

qplot(xmin=t, xmax=tend, ymin=d-0.45, ymax=d+0.45, data=inc,
geom="rect", fill=act) + scale_y_reverse("Day", breaks = 1:2) +
scale_x_continuous("Time") + scale_colour_manual(name = "Activity",
values=c("red","blue","green"), breaks = c("?","off","on"), labels =
c("Not recorded", "Off nest", "On Nest"))

But no dice--it's just giving me default colors of some sort. A clue
seems to be that in the first plot, the legend is correctly labeled
(with the name and labels argument from the scale parameter), but in
the second plot, the legend is formed by the column header and levels
in that column...

Any help would be appreciated. Thanks!

Eliot

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: scale colour question
parts:
Hi Elliot,
fill and color are separate aesthetics. In the second example you need
scale_fill_manual ...

Best,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: scale colour question
parts: Thank you very much. The very slightly modified code

qplot(xmin=t, xmax=tend, ymin=d-0.45, ymax=d+0.45, data=inc,
geom="rect", fill=act) + scale_y_reverse("Day", breaks = 1:2) +

runs just fine. Don't worry, I won't keep those horrendous colors.

Cheers,
Eliot
